text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Service="infer-streaming" p99 latency breached SLO (p99=2.35s > 1.0s) — continuous-batching execution path high tail latency. Paging @oncall. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/services/infer-streaming?panel=streaming-p99

Aisha: On it. I'm paging SRE and ML runtime, grabbing traces and recent deploys. Any recent config flips to batching?

Rajan: Not aware of config flips. Scheduler metrics show a sudden growth in queued small-seqlen jobs hitting a continuous batcher bin. Looking.

Emilia: I see correlated streaming stalls in KV-cache hot misses and long wait times in batch-coalesce. p95 also creeping up. Adding logs.

Aisha: Quick customer impact check — Support, could you surface any customer tickets or Correlate with 5xx/stream-drop alerts?

Support: We're seeing increased call durations for streaming endpoints and 2 customer sessions timed out (Acme Corp, Plume). Errors are timeouts, not 500s. Rate of streaming stalls ~4% of requests in last 10m.

Matt: Posting quick traces:
```
trace_id: 0x9f3
span: scheduler_enqueue -> batch_coalesce (wait 230ms) -> runtime_launch (gpu wait 50ms) -> kvcache_miss_fetch (180ms)
```
Looks like mixing very short and very long sequences is causing head-of-line waiting in the continuous batcher.

Rajan: I can reproduce locally with a mixed-seqlen load: many short seqs + occasional long seq pushes batch size high then serialization stalls streaming frames. Batcher fairness is currently size-prioritized, no preemption.

Aisha: Mitigations we can try (fast):
- Option A: Disable continuous batching for streaming route (will fall back to immediate small batches).
- Option B: Set max_cont_batch_size to lower (e.g., 8 -> 4) and enable per-queue fairness preemption.
- Option C: Temporarily pin streaming traffic to the short-seqlen optimized kernel variant (model-small-window)

Emilia: I can roll a config patch to set max_cont_batch_size=4 and enable fairness token-shed for continuous-batcher. Patch ready, will push if oncall approves.

Aisha: Do it. Start with lowering batch size to reduce head-of-line. If that doesn't recover p99 within 5m, disable continuous batching for streaming endpoints. Notify customers.

Rajan: Pushing config via /deploy-config now:
```
kubectl set env deployment/infer-runtime CONT_BATCH_MAX=4 CONT_BATCH_FAIRNESS=true -n prod
```
Rolling update started.

ops-bot: Deploy job 8732 started by Rajan; status: in-progress.

(2m later)
ops-bot: Deploy job 8732 succeeded on 90% of pods; new env applied.

Emilia: Metrics are showing p99 dropping from 2.35s -> 1.1s after patch, p95 stable. Still above SLO but trending.

Aisha: Good. Hold patch, watch for 10m. If still >1.0s, we will disable continuous batching on streaming.

Support: Notifying affected customers (Acme, Plume) that we're investigating latency; ETA unknown.

(8m later)
Emilia: p99 = 0.98s now (last 5m). Streaming stalls reduced to 0.6% of requests. Looks recovered.

Rajan: Checked allocator and scheduler traces — fairness tokens prevented long seqs from monopolizing continuous batches. The preemption patch works.

Aisha: Ok let's keep max batch size = 4 and fairness enabled for the next 24h while we tune. Create follow-up runbook item to:
- Run mixed-seqlen chaos test to validate thresholds.
- Add a dynamic knob to auto-shrink batch size when short-seq ratio > X.
- Add streaming-specific cache warmup for KV misses to reduce cold-miss penalty.

Matt: I'll open a PR with automated test and a stress harness for mixed sequences. Also propose telemetry: track short-vs-long ratio per queue and batch-occupancy percentiles.

Support: Customers informed that incident mitigated; monitoring for recurrence.

Aisha: Handoff to night on-call (Rajan) at 23:00 UTC. Please watch the following dashboards: streaming-p99, continuous-batcher-occupancy, kvcache-miss-rate. If p99 > 1.2s for 3 consecutive 5m windows, escalate to SRE pager and follow rollback plan.

Rajan: Acknowledged. I'll monitor and have a playbook to disable continuous batching for streaming if we see regression.

Emilia: Filed a post-incident work item: 
- ID: PBI-1184
- Title: continuous-batcher fairness + adaptive shrink for mixed seq-length workloads
- Notes: include telemetry, unit tests, and a canary rollout plan.

Aisha: Thanks team. Closing the urgent paging loop. Will keep an eye and re-open if trend reverses. :white_check_mark:
